_meta.readme: Pinned phase-2 MCP tool surfaces. `./bench.sh capture` compares the live surfaces against this file and FAILS on any difference, because a tool surface is the defining cost of a front-loaded condition and a spec or schema change moves it silently. PHASE2_PLAN.md §8.1 quotes these numbers; this file owns them. To change one deliberately: re-run capture, read the diff it prints, update the value here and the §8.1 table in the same commit.
_meta.why_phase_2_only: Phase 1's A1/A2/B/B2 surfaces come from GitHub's live MCP server and live GraphQL schema, so they cannot be pinned — re-measuring would compare against today's upstream, not June's (§11). Phase 2's are generated from hash-pinned local fixtures, so they are exactly reproducible and there is no excuse for letting them drift.
_meta.tools_list_bytes: len(json.dumps(tools/list result)) as recorded by capture/capture_mcp.py

M-R1.note: Was 9,440 when §8.1 was first written on 2026-08-28. Commit 14d8973 added a `roles` filter to the assignments endpoint on both surfaces, which grew listAssignment's inputSchema by 161 bytes. A real change, correctly reflected — and it sat unnoticed until this baseline existed, which is the argument for the baseline. Note the asymmetry it illustrates rather than violates: adding an API capability grows a front-loaded tool surface and leaves an on-demand one untouched (M-R2, M-G1 unchanged), while GraphQL's frozen operations absorbed it at zero prefix cost.

M-G1.note: Within 13% of M-R2 by design — these two are the clean protocol pair, so they share tool count, shape, and search-then-execute grammar. If that gap widens, the protocol comparison has acquired a tool-packaging confound and needs re-reading before publishing.

M-G2.note: One tool per frozen operation in services/operations/. src/test/operations.test.ts already fails if that set changes; this catches the other direction — Apollo MCP rendering the same operations into a different schema after a version bump.
